## TL;DR

Task #1061 stops RepoOS bookkeeping from invalidating a running check. Handoff and managed engineer checks now take an advisory worktree lock. Bookkeeping commits on the task branch (`work/**`, `.repoos/**`) are deferred until the gate ends and flushed in order; source commits are refused with named paths and commit subjects. HEAD-drift detection uses shared `checkGateHeadDriftAllowed` logic (bookkeeping-only, WIP checkpoint chains, fail-closed). Docs updated in `user-docs/check.md` and `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md`. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed after build.

## Work and rationale

The incident was repeated handoff failures: `the worktree changed while the gate was running` while long checks ran. Root cause was HEAD moving on the task branch from server bookkeeping (task file activity, reports, engineering report staging) and occasionally from WIP checkpoint semantics, even though those paths cannot change build or test outcomes.

Previous drift logic in `describeStateDrift` only ignored commits touching the task's own `work/<id>-*.md` file, not `work/reports/**` or `.repoos/**`, and gave no detail about which commit moved source.

I introduced `src/core/check-gate-bookkeeping.ts` for path classification and drift analysis, and `src/server/check-gate-lock.ts` for the advisory lock, deferred-commit queue on disk, hook integration via `setCheckGateCommitHook`, and stale-lock recovery on server start. `commitFiles` calls the hook: defer bookkeeping on a locked worktree, refuse source, proceed otherwise. Handoff acquires the lock after the pre-check snapshot and releases it in `finally` so every exit path flushes the queue. Managed `repoos check` (`REPOOS_AGENT=1`) installs the same hook and lock for engineer self-check.

## Approaches tried

I extended the existing review-lock pattern rather than a new global mutex. Deferring commits instead of suppressing task-file writes keeps Activity and report content on disk while HEAD stays fixed for the gate. Fail-closed behavior when `pathsChangedBetweenCommits` returns null is preserved and surfaced in the refusal text.

## Challenges and blockers

Merge-gate close-out checks share the same class of problem but the orchestrator path is large; this change covers handoff-finalize and engineer self-check explicitly. Close-out merge-gate lock wiring can follow the same `acquireCheckGateLock` / `releaseCheckGateLock` pair around its local `repoos check` child.

Cross-process engineer file writes are still caught by the drift guard on uncommitted work files; commit-time refusal carries the specified user-facing message.

## Key learnings

Centralizing "what invalidates a check" in one module avoids a third parallel allowlist (handoff, close-out, review already had related rules). Persisting the deferred queue under `.repoos/check-gate-deferred/` makes crash recovery testable without inventing a new DB. Using `REPOOS_CHECK_GATE_INTERNAL` during flush prevents re-entrant deferral when applying the queue.
